prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Conservative Party Manifesto 1997 – Summary (under 500 words)

Core argument
- Build on 1979–97 reforms that, the party claims, delivered low inflation, falling unemployment, industrial peace, inward investment and lower taxes. Warns against “European social model” and state expansion. Goal: make Britain the Enterprise Centre of Europe while preserving national sovereignty and constitutional stability.

Economy and business
- Keep public spending growth below economic growth; aim to reduce it below 40% of GDP and move toward a balanced budget by 2000.
- Tax: maintain Europe’s lowest tax burden; target a 20p basic income tax rate and cap the top rate at 40p.
- Prices: maintain 2.5% inflation target; keep mortgage rates low.
- Jobs: reject EU Social Chapter, minimum wage and new EU employment burdens; expand welfare-to-work (Project Work nationwide; “Britain Works”).
- Small firms: cut small companies’ corporation tax alongside personal tax cuts; reduce capital taxes when prudent; reform business rates to ease small-business costs; expand deregulation and “sunset” clauses.
- Competition and trade: new Competition Bill; push single market completion, global free trade by 2020; promote IT leadership and “IT for All”; connect schools, libraries via Millennium Fund.

Families, ownership and welfare
- Family tax reform: allow transfer of unused personal allowance to a working spouse when caring for children/dependants (worth up to ~£17.50/week).
- Savings and pensions: expand employee share ownership; raise inheritance tax thresholds prudently; major reform to give new workers funded personal pension accounts via NI rebates, with a state pension guarantee.
- Social services: new statutory framework, openness and regulation across sectors; vouchers/direct payments; respite care for carers; long-term care partnership.
- Social security: protect Child Benefit/Family Credit; align lone-parent benefits; intensify anti-fraud measures.

Education
- Education Guarantee: national targets, published test results (including age 7 and 14; baseline at 5), rigorous standards (spelling/grammar, no overuse of calculators), intervention in failing schools/LEAs, stronger discipline, teacher appraisal linked to outcomes.
- Choice/diversity: maintain nursery vouchers; expand Assisted Places; more grant-maintained and self-governing schools; more specialist schools; allow some selection and new grammar schools where parents want them.
- Post-16: learning credits 14–21; expand Modern Apprenticeships; uphold A-levels; support HE/FE standards.

Health and public services
- NHS: real-terms increases each year; shorter waits; more information on outcomes; expand GP fundholding and primary care (nurse prescribing); invest via Private Finance Initiative; strengthen mental health services; continue Health of the Nation prevention.
- Public service reform: Citizens’ Charter, more competition/privatisation (extend gas competition; consider Royal Mail options; privatise Parcelforce; privatise National Air Traffic Services), challenge funding in local government; compulsory competitive tendering; curb disruptive strikes in essential services.
- Transport: complete rail privatisation; privatise and modernise London Underground with fare caps; invest in roads via PFI; support regional airports; improve safety.

Law and order
- More police and CCTV; voluntary ID card linked to photo driving licence; tough on juvenile crime (parental control orders, curfews, reparation); national crime squad; mandatory minimums for repeat violent/sexual offenders, drug dealers and burglars; end automatic early release; stronger victim protections; faster justice; legal aid within cash limits; tough anti-drugs strategy.

Nation, environment and countryside
- Regenerate worst estates via tenant-led transfers and private capital; extend Rough Sleeper Initiative; protect green belt; prioritise brownfield housing; support rural shops and jobs; resist general right to roam; aim to double forest cover.
- Agriculture/fisheries: support beef sector/BSE eradication; food safety adviser/council; CAP reform; defend quotas/limits; raise animal welfare.
- Environment: improve air/water quality; cleaner vehicles; polluter-pays.

Foreign affairs, Europe and defence
- Global engagement via UN, NATO, Commonwealth; climate leadership; focused aid and debt relief.
- Europe: partnership of nation states; keep veto, border controls, budget rebate; oppose Social Chapter/extra costs; back enlargement and flexibility.
- Single currency: keep options open; likely not 1999; any entry only after a national referendum.
- Defence: maintain strong professional forces, Trident, rapid deployment; no review; support reserves and cadets.

Constitution and Union
- Evolution not revolution: more open government, better parliamentary process (two-year legislative planning); oppose PR/Bill of Rights; resist devolution that risks the Union; pursue NI talks with security against terrorism.
